title: The 50 most-played Steam Next Fest demos include 7 incremental games, 4 AI disclosures, and only one instance of haystack slop
summary: Ten years ago, this list would have shocked most PC gamers.
body: Last week's Steam Next Fest had over 8,000 demos; now Valve has revealed the 50 most-played among them. The results aren't surprising: there's lots of friendsloppy casual co-op, incremental games continue to be popular, and players have by-and-large rejected games with overt generative AI use, with only four of the games among the 50 declaring AI use in development. Here are some other factoids: 7 incremental games, including 10 Million Pixels and Unharvest 15 lighthearted or comedic co-op games (aka friendslop) including Dude, Trust Me , Oar'Some Adventures , and Banana Airways 3 survival games including Frostrail , Never Be Alone and Arctic Drive 3 games that self-describe as "cozy" including Loftia 1 MMO in ArchAge Chronicles 1 haystack slop game Among all 50 of these games, the only entry published by a traditional "blockbuster" publisher was Tropico 7, a Ubisoft affair [Oops, it's actually a Kalypso Media affair]. Teach My Little Sister How To Drive was one of the four games with AI disclosures. It leans heavily on an LLM-powered NPC which apparently cost its developer over $1,000 a day . title: The best haunted card game since Inscryption is back with a new mystery only solitaire freaks can solve
summary: Forbidden Solitaire's The Discarded DLC is here and those cards aren't going to play themselves.
body: The first new card I found in Forbidden Solitaire's new DLC The Discarded gave me the power to throw a card like a knife at whatever horror was trying to kill me. Although nothing warranted such a desperate move, I fear it won't be long before I find myself out of options now that I've seen the devilish new tricks the developers have dealt in the DLC's first hour. I'm lucky I just spent the last week playing through the base game because The Discarded offers no help: From the moment you double click the DLC executable on the game's '90s-inspired PC interface, you're on your own. It's not quite enough to understand how to play solitaire; you need to know how to play Forbidden Solitaire , a haunted version of the classic card game where you must change your approach based on the modified cards the developers throw at you. Some cards might be locked away until you play the right suits. Others might be surrounded by bones, requiring them to be played twice before leaving the board. Your deck will run out quickly if you don't strategize around these factors and try to knock off as many cards as you can in one turn. Thankfully, you can cheat… by jamming gems into your flesh. Walter Koenig, Star Trek's Pavel Chekhov, has died
summary: Koenig gained fame as the Russian navigator of the USS Enterprise in the original Star Trek television series, films, and games.
body: A Variety report says that Walter Koenig, known to the world as Star Trek's Russian hothead Pavel Chekhov, has died. Koenig's big break in show biz came in 1967, when he was cast as Chekhov in the second season of the original Star Trek series. He portrayed the character until the show's cancellation, and then through seven feature films; he had a particularly memorable scene in Star Trek 2: The Wrath of Khan, when a Ceti eel burrowed its way into his brain. Even now, it's pretty gnarly. The downside of that early-career fame is that Koenig was typecast, and acting roles following the end of the Star Trek series were sparse. He turned to screenwriting through the 1970s; ironically, while the character of Chekhov was not included in the Star Trek animated series that ran for two seasons after the live-action show was cancelled, he wrote the script for an animated series episode called The Infinite Vulcan, making him the first member of the cast to write an episode for the Star Trek franchise. But Koenig also played very much against type in at least one memorable role: Alfred Bester, a powerful Psi Corps officer in Babylon 5. Where Chekhov was brash, good-hearted, and a little naiv…

title: CD Projekt marks the 19th anniversary of its first Witcher RPG with a tribute to BioWare: 'Their support helped turn our vision into Geralt’s first interactive adventure'
summary: The Witcher was developed on BioWare's Aurora engine, but the Dragon Age studio did more than just share its tech.
body: Today, October 26, is the 19 th anniversary of The Witcher, the groundbreaking RPG that introduced Geralt, and CD Projekt, to the world. To mark the moment, CD Projekt took to social to pay tribute to friends who made it all possible: BioWare. CD Projekt joint CEO Michał Nowakowski spoke warmly of BioWare last week in the immediate aftermath of the studio's shocking closure , crediting it as "a massive part of CDPR history." The Witcher was built on BioWare's Aurora engine, which it created for Neverwinter Nights, but BioWare did more than just share technology: It also worked to help bring the upstart Polish RPG to much wider attention. "19 years ago, an ambitious dream to bring an iconic book series into the world of video games came to life with the release of The Witcher. It was the start of an unforgettable path, which wouldn't have been possible without our friends at BioWare," CD Projekt wrote. "From lending us their Aurora Engine and sharing their knowledge, to giving us a spot at their booth at E3, their support helped turn our vision into Geralt’s first interactive adventure. Thank you to everyone who has walked the Path with us from the very beginning. Happy 19th annive…

title: New Windows 11 Insider Experimental build adds the ability to check your internet speed without a browser
summary: A small change, but a handy one.
body: If you are part of the Windows 11 Insider program, you may have finally received the option to test your internet speed directly from Quick Settings in the latest experimental build. That means no more going to a browser to see if your new broadband package is as speedy as advertised. Those using Insider Experimental build 26340.9767 can simply click on Quick Settings and scroll down to see a speed test button (via Windows Latest ). You can also find the network icon in the system tray, right-click it, and then select "Test internet speed". This will give you your download and upload speeds. Up until now, Windows 11 users have been able to access an internet speed test from Windows settings, but clicking on it redirects you to a browser and then runs the test via Bing. It's a small barrier but still an annoying hurdle to get to a fairly simple tool. Alongside this, Preview Build 26340.9767 adds feature flags (so you can filter your machine by which options are enabled / disabled), Quick Settings now gives access to mobile phones, it adds a Magnifier keyboard shortcut, it gives an easier way to access your Microsoft 365 subscription, and a few other things. summary: Cool, I'll get right on it.
body: If you've watched as many Sam Altman interviews as I have, you'll know he's not shy when it comes to recounting a previously held opinion. Speaking at the Stanford Graduate School of Business last week , the OpenAI CEO spoke about AI safety, particularly in regards to cybersecurity. "The cybersecurity..." Altman begins, before pausing. "I don't even know a dramatic enough word to use... but the problem coming towards us is still something that we have not, as organizational leaders, or countries, or individuals taken seriously." "There was a moment earlier this year where... it was like the Mythos freak out, or whatever people called it, and I think things did get somewhat better. Like, people definitely patched some bugs," the OpenAI CEO continues. "But it was another one of these cases where people didn't really intuit the exponential." "I don't think most people said, okay, the models are going to get much smarter," says Altman. "They can probably find bugs, like crazy bugs, you know, bugs that are outside of the normal threat model of what we think a hacker can do. title: Leaked video shows hundreds, possibly thousands of brand-new RTX 5090s being dismantled for AI server usage in Chinese factory
summary: So that's where they're going.
body: Consumer RTX 5090 stock in the US (and many other countries) seems to be virtually non-existent at the moment, despite Nvidia's claims that production is still ongoing . So, what's happening to all those brand new consumer cards? A leaked video reportedly taken from inside a Chinese factory may have the answer. title: Korean police arrest cyberhacking gang reportedly led by self-taught hacker, who allegedly used AI to breach 60 firms and received a mere $210 in ransom
summary: In this case, crime really didn't pay. Much.
body: As AI continues to get smarter, the schemes using it have often become more successful. However, one South Korean cyberhacking gang, reportedly led by a self-taught hacker using AI tools, doesn't seem to have made off with a king's ransom. Despite allegedly obtaining 8.2 million records and demanding 360,000,000 Won (around $271.77K) from victims, the gang is said to have ended up receiving 300,000 Won (around $210). This is according to Yonhap News Agency , Seoul Economic Daily , and The Chosun Daily , which corroborate reports. Altogether, the gang reportedly accessed files from over 90 firms, but 60 successful hits came from hacks using AI tools (a mixture of AI coding and an autonomous penetration testing system). The stolen data is said to have included customer information like names, registration numbers, phone numbers, and addresses. The cyberhacking gang is also said to have sent threatening emails to those affected, saying, "If the data breach becomes public, the company’s reputation will be damaged, and government fines may be imposed." Payment info was not caught up in these breaches, and South Korean police say stolen data has not yet made it onto the dark web. As not…

summary: You can say that again.
body: As reported by IGN , veteran actors Jennifer Hale and Mark Meer, who voiced the female and male Commanders Shepard in Mass Effect, respectively, directly addressed fans of the series in an October 21 Instagram Live . The two reflected on BioWare, and commiserated over its tragic fate. Here are some highlights from each I pulled from the stream: Both actors' reactions strike me as so characteristic of their respective backgrounds: Hale is one of the voices of videogames (not to diminish Meer's own extensive resume). She jumped to BioWare's place in the industry and its current crisis. Meer, a standby of the Edmonton theater and improv scene, fixated on the closure's effects on this city he clearly loves. Both are 100% correct about the collective joy and meaning people found in BioWare's work. That's something private equity can't take from us ⁠—at least not with current technology. As for Hale's optimism regarding the rights and potential future of the franchise, well, I Want To Believe. title: Overwatch devs took one look at Jetpack Cat and Bastion's combo and went 'oh, that's a little scary'
summary: The Apache helicopter meta was certainly something to be feared.
body: Almost a year ago now, Team 4 debuted a new kind of Overwatch , and as part of the huge spotlight we learned that the live service FPS would undergo a new cadence with yearly themes comprising several seasons. Five new heroes were also added straight away; Mizuki, Emre, Anran, Domina, and of course Jetpack Cat. Ahead of being added to the game, Overwatch's community was overjoyed to see Jetpack Cat, an adorable little ginger kitty in a flying mech—what's not to love? But sentiment quickly shifted after she took to the battlefield. Jetpack Cat broke the game with her new Apache helicopter meta which saw her haul Bastion high into the air so he could gun down the entire enemy team while in turret mode, it was truly horrific. (Image credit: Blizzard Entertainment) Who could've predicted that the adorable little cat would cause so much havoc? Well Team 4 had an inkling while Jetpack Cat was in the testing phase. title: Mass Effect 5 would have let players generate alternate timelines based on their choices in previous games, according to the series' technical director
summary: "You had so many choices that you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes," Romain Toutain explained in a livestream.
body: The more information that dribbles out from BioWare's cancelled Mass Effect game, the sadder I feel about the whole sorry situation. We've already seen an in-engine trailer that introduced a new protagonist and reintroduced Liara T'Soni, and we've heard that the game was set in a 'galactic Cold War' that combined all three of Mass Effect 3 's possible endings. Now, it seems the new Mass Effect would also have had a sophisticated system for dealing with the choices players made in the original trilogy. This is according to Mass Effect's Franchise Technical Director Romain Toutain, who ran a Twitch stream during which he provided commentary on the recently leaked trailer, offering some insight into the game that trailer was supposed to reveal (via Kotaku ). Although the stream was in French, a clip was posted on Bluesky by user @loustica-lucia, who added English subtitles to Toutain's commentary. During his stream, Toutain mentions that BioWare was working on a novel way to account for the many choices players made while playing the Mass Effect trilogy, pointing out that "all of the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taking into account." title: Award-winning sci-fi author NK Jemisin joins BioWare's mourners and scorns a broken industry for killing geese that 'laid the golden eggs'
summary: "The [Mass Effect] and [Dragon Age] games were a literal inspiration."
body: The death of BioWare has provoked a whole lot of tributes, memorialisation, and plain old nostalgia as all sorts of people come together to remember the bangers the erstwhile king of RPGs put out in its prime. CD Projekt Red , imsim founding father Warren Spector , and we here at PCG have all been trading BioWare memories (and sometimes lamenting the influence of EA, which acquired the studio back in 2007). But the BioWare classics were big enough bangers to transcend videogames in their influence. Over on Bluesky , award-winning sci-fi and fantasy writer Nora Jemisin (better known as NK Jemisin) has been mourning the studio too. "RIP Bioware. The [Mass Effect] and [Dragon Age] games were a literal inspiration, and I can't count how many times I've replayed my faves," Jemisin wrote. "I made lifelong friends on ME3 Multiplayer. I still think Jennifer Hepler is the best game writer I've seen, and Jennifer Hale's the best VA." Hepler was a long-time Dragon Age writer who " was pretty much in charge of the dwarf origin story " in Origins, and also shaped much of the setting's dwarven culture in general. Jennifer Hale, meanwhile, is Jennifer Hale: Dynaheir, Mazzy Fentan, Bastila Shan, …
